translationRepairs: After Taizu accepted the throne, Pu was made Right Remonstrance Grandee and Hanlin Academician of the Privy Council for his founding service.
After Taizu accepted the throne, Pu was made Right Remonstrance Grandee and Academician of the Privy Council for his founding service.
The Chinese appoints him 樞密直學士, a Privy Council academician; 翰林 is not in the sentence, so Hanlin is an invented office.
When he accepted the mandate, Pu, for his merit in founding the dynasty, was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and Hanlin Academician of the Privy Council.
When he accepted the mandate, Pu, for his merit in founding the dynasty, was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and Academician of the Privy Council.
The literal English likewise inserts Hanlin; 充樞密直學士 is Academician of the Privy Council, not a Hanlin post.
In the third year of Jianlong, he was made Commissioner of the Privy Council and Acting Grand Preceptor.
In the third year of Jianlong, he was made Commissioner of the Privy Council and Acting Grand Guardian.
檢校太保 is the honorary Grand Guardian; Grand Preceptor would be 太師, a different Three Dukes title.
In the third year of Jianlong, he was appointed Commissioner of the Privy Council and Acting Grand Preceptor.
In the third year of Jianlong, he was appointed Commissioner of the Privy Council and Acting Grand Guardian.
The same office 檢校太保 must be Acting Grand Guardian in the literal rendering, not Grand Preceptor.

Private sale of timber from Qin and Long was forbidden; Pu sent a trusted clerk to buy building timber, and linked great rafts to bring it to the capital for his mansion; the clerk smuggled timber on the side, falsely claiming it was Pu's purchase, and sold it in the capital; Zhao Pin, commissioner of the three departments, investigated and reported it.

Private sale of timber from Qin and Long was forbidden; Pu sent a trusted clerk to buy building timber, and linked great rafts to bring it to the capital for his mansion; the clerk smuggled timber on the side, falsely claiming it was Pu's purchase, and sold it in the capital; Zhao Pin, acting commissioner of the three departments, investigated and reported it.
權三司使 marks Zhao Pin as acting commissioner of the Three Departments; omitting 權 overstates the tenure.
Formerly Prince Qin Tingmei had ranked above the chancellor; now, as an old founding minister restored to high office, Pu asked to rank below him, and the request was granted.

Formerly Prince Qin Tingmei had ranked above the chancellor; now, because Pu was an old founding minister restored to chief minister, Tingmei submitted a memorial asking to rank below him, and the request was granted.
The topic remains 秦王廷美; 以普勳舊，再登元輔 explains why Tingmei 表乞居其下, yielding precedence to restored chancellor Pu, not Pu asking to stand below him.

Previously Prince Qin Tingmei had ranked above the chancellor; now, because Pu was an old merit-holder who again ascended to chief minister, he memorialized asking to rank below Tingmei, and the request was granted.

Previously Prince Qin Tingmei had ranked above the chancellor; now, because Pu was an old merit-holder who again ascended to chief minister, Tingmei memorialized asking to rank below him, and the request was granted.
The silent subject of 表乞居其下 is Tingmei, who asks to rank below Pu; the original literal makes Pu petition to stand below Tingmei.

I have studied the classics and know the precedents: the memorials of Zhufu Yan, Xu Yue, and Yan An in Emperor Wu's Han, and the ten counsels Chancellor Yao Yuanchong offered Emperor Ming of Tang—loyal, penetrating arguments fit to be enacted.

I have studied the classics and know the precedents: the memorials of Zhufu Yan, Xu Yue, and Yan An in the time of Emperor Wu of Han, and the ten counsels Chancellor Yao Yuanchong offered Emperor Ming of Tang—loyal, penetrating arguments fit to be enacted.
漢武時 is a temporal phrase, the time of Emperor Wu of Han; “Emperor Wu's Han” misreads 時 as a possessive dynasty name.

When the plowing rites concluded, Taizong wished to appoint Lü Mengzheng chief minister. Because Lü was newly risen, he drew on Pu's established stature as a model and invested Pu as Grand Preceptor and concurrently Palace Secretariat Director.

When the plowing rites concluded, Taizong wished to appoint Lü Mengzheng chief minister. Because Lü was newly risen, he drew on Pu's established stature as a model and invested Pu as Grand Guardian and concurrently Palace Secretariat Director.
冊拜太保兼侍中 invests Pu as Grand Guardian concurrently Palace Secretariat Director; Grand Preceptor is 太師, conferred later.

When the sacred-field rites were complete, Taizong wished to make Lü Mengzheng chief minister; because he was newly advanced, he relied on Pu's old virtue as a model, and invested him as Grand Preceptor concurrently Palace Secretariat Director.

When the sacred-field rites were complete, Taizong wished to make Lü Mengzheng chief minister; because he was newly advanced, he relied on Pu's old virtue as a model, and invested him as Grand Guardian concurrently Palace Secretariat Director.
The literal likewise conflates 太保 with Grand Preceptor; the Chinese title is Grand Guardian.
His hatred of the forceful and upright took this form throughout.
His hatred of evil and his firm uprightness were all of this kind.
嫉惡強直 praises hating evil while remaining firmly upright; “hatred of the forceful and upright” reverses the historian’s judgment.
When Li Jiqian troubled the frontier, Pu proposed that Zhao Baozhong be restored to his old lands in Xiatang, and ordered a plot accordingly.
When Li Jiqian troubled the frontier, Pu proposed that Zhao Baozhong be restored to his old Xia lands, and ordered a plot accordingly.
夏臺 is the Xia territorial name, not a toponym Xiatang; the idiomatic already has Xia lands.

Pu declared his illness grave and thrice memorialized to retire. The Emperor reluctantly agreed, appointing him Administrator of the Western Capital and Intendant of Henan while retaining his titles of Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat.

Pu declared his illness grave and thrice memorialized to retire. The Emperor reluctantly agreed, appointing him Administrator of the Western Capital and Intendant of Henan while retaining his titles of Grand Guardian and Director of the Secretariat.
依前守太保兼中書令 keeps the Grand Guardian title already held; it is not 太師.

In spring of the third year of Chunhua, aged and long ill, he had Liu Changyan, acting administrator and vice-prefect, submit a memorial requesting retirement. Imperial emissaries raced by relay to inquire after him. In all he thrice begged to retire.

In spring of the third year of Chunhua, aged and long ill, he had Liu Changyan, vice-prefect attached to the Western Capital administration, submit a memorial requesting retirement. Imperial emissaries raced by relay to inquire after him. In all he thrice begged to retire.
留守通判 is the tongpan under the Western Capital administration; Liu Changyan is not himself the acting administrator.

A special emissary was again dispatched with an edict for Pu: "You recently fell ill and earnestly sought to retire. Given the weight of my duties, I feared to burden you in your old age. The title of Grand Preceptor was meant to honor your worth.

A special emissary was again dispatched with an edict for Pu: "You recently fell ill and earnestly sought to retire. Given the weight of remaining as capital guardian, I feared to burden you in your old age. The title of Grand Preceptor was meant to honor your worth.
朕以居守之重 refers to the burden of Pu’s capital-guardian post (西京留守), not the emperor’s own duties.
He said to close ministers: Pu served the previous emperor, was an old acquaintance of mine, could decide great affairs; formerly he and I had our shortcomings—all know this.
He said to close ministers: Pu served the previous emperor, was an old acquaintance of mine, could decide great affairs; formerly he and I had our differences—all know this.
嚮與朕嘗有不足 names prior friction between emperor and minister; “shortcomings” invents a moral failing the Chinese does not state.

When Taizong took the throne he put an end to De Chao's slander and came to suspect Cao Bin of disloyalty. With Pu again as chief minister, Pu spoke in Bin's defense and cleared his name—the facts spoke for themselves.
Taizong gave ear to De Chao's slander and suspected Cao Bin of disloyalty. When Pu was again chief minister, he spoke in Bin's defense and cleared his name—the facts spoke for themselves.
太宗入弭德超之讒 is Taizong taking in Mi Dechao’s slander, not accession and not putting the slander to an end; s0205–s0206 confirm he had been misled.
When Taizong ascended the throne he quelled De Chao's slander, suspected Cao Bin of improper conduct, and entrusted Pu again as chief minister; Pu cleared and vouched for Bin—the facts were clear.
Taizong accepted Mi Dechao's slander, suspected Cao Bin of improper conduct, and, with Pu again as chief minister, Pu cleared and vouched for Bin—the facts were clear.
入弭德超之讒 is being taken in by Mi Dechao’s slander; 入 is not “ascended the throne,” and 弭 is the surname, not a verb “quell.”
Pu memorialized: "Corrupt officials who merit punishment should properly face execution.
Pu memorialized: "An official who betrays his office and merits punishment should properly face the penal statutes.
宜正刑辟 calls for applying the penal statutes; 刑辟 is not specifically execution, which the original literal invents.
When Cao Shen was appointed prefect, Anyi was transferred to vice prefect; shortly afterward he was relieved and recalled.
When Cao Can was appointed prefect, Anyi was transferred to vice prefect; shortly afterward he was relieved and recalled.
曹璨 is the Song figure Cao Can; Cao Shen renders 曹參 and names the wrong person.
When Cao Shen was made prefect, Anyi was transferred to be vice prefect; before long he was relieved and returned.
When Cao Can was made prefect, Anyi was transferred to be vice prefect; before long he was relieved and returned.
The literal likewise misnames 曹璨 as Cao Shen; Cao Can is the required English form.
He was twice transferred to investigating officer of Henan Prefecture.
He was promoted again to investigating officer of Henan Prefecture.
再遷河南府推官 is a further promotion ending in that post, not two appointments to the same Henan office.

Only until the third year of Zhidao, going west to the mausoleum, after the rites were complete, then bearing the yu tablet back to the capital, exchanging for the spirit tablet and enshrining in the temple—to accord with canonical rites.'

Not until the third year of Zhidao, going west to the mausoleum, after the rites were complete, then bearing the yu tablet back to the capital, exchanging for the spirit tablet and enshrining in the temple—to accord with canonical rites.'
直至至道三年 means the delayed rites happened only then; “Only until” reverses the temporal force of 直至.
Anyi is absurd and ignorant, citing precedents at random, comparing a dafu relative to three-year mourning, and deceiving his sovereign to this extent.
Anyi is absurd and ignorant, citing precedents at random, comparing a relative in the da-gong grade of mourning to the three-year mourning regulation, and deceiving his sovereign to this extent.
大功之親 is kin in the nine-month da-gong mourning grade, not a dafu; the comparison is to 三年之制.
